intent: Let the user press one or several of a small set of related options drawn as toggle buttons that share one pressed state.
typical_uses: A switch between a few mutually exclusive modes of the same content (alignment, view mode)
A row of independent formatting or filter marks that may be pressed together

dont_use_when.situation: A single on/off control with no sibling options
Each choice shows its own panel of content
A form field picking one of several labelled options
A row of one-shot actions with no pressed state

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

`value`, `defaultValue` and the value `onValueChange` receives are arrays of item values with and without `multiple`. Without `multiple`, pressing an item yields a one-element array and pressing the pressed item again yields an empty array.
Setting `disabled` on the group disables every item inside it; an item's own `disabled` can disable that one item further but cannot re-enable it against a disabled group.
`variant`, `size` and `iconOnly` set on the group apply to every item and win over the item's own; an item's own value applies only where the group leaves that prop unset.

anti_patterns.dont: Render the group with no accessible name
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at a visible heading; a `<label htmlFor>` cannot name the group, because the group is a div with role="group", not a labelable element

a11y.by: The primitive's ToggleGroup (role="group" and arrow-key roving focus between items, with Home/End and wrap-around by default) plus toggle-group.test.tsx's getByRole('group', { name }) assertion on the aria-labelled group

value.states: value is an array of the caller's own Value type parameter, one entry per pressed item
value.because: Base UI types it as `readonly Value[]`, where `Value extends string` is the caller's own type parameter; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so the caller's narrowing is checked by tsc, not by the schema.

defaultValue.states: defaultValue is an array of the caller's own Value type parameter, the initially pressed items
defaultValue.because: Same `readonly Value[]` type as `value`, for the uncontrolled starting state; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so the caller's narrowing is checked by tsc, not by the schema.

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a callback of the next array of pressed item values and event details
onValueChange.because: Base UI types it as `(groupValue: Value[], eventDetails) => void`; a function has no JSON Schema representation, so nothing beyond its presence is asserted.

style.states: style is a plain React style object; when `spacing` is set, its gap replaces any gap given here
style.because: ToggleGroupProps omits Base UI's `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` style and redeclares it as React's `CSSProperties`, so the function form is not accepted; the compiler has no JSON type for `CSSProperties`, so nothing is asserted. The kit's own styling goes through toggle-group.module.css, not through this.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the group's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

good.title: Single selection kept to one chosen option
good.code:
<ToggleGroup value={[view]} onValueChange={([next]) => next && setView(next)} aria-label="View">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="list" aria-label="List"><ListIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="grid" aria-label="Grid"><GridIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>

good.title: Multiple selection, uncontrolled
good.code:
<ToggleGroup multiple defaultValue={['bold']} variant="outline" aria-label="Text formatting">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold"><BoldIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic"><ItalicIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>

good.title: Joined icon strip
good.code:
<ToggleGroup spacing={0} variant="outline" size="sm" iconOnly defaultValue={['list']} aria-label="View">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="list" aria-label="List"><ListIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="grid" aria-label="Grid"><GridIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>

bad.title: A single-selection value passed as a plain string
bad.code:
<ToggleGroup value={align} onValueChange={setAlign} aria-label="Alignment">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="left" aria-label="Left"><AlignLeftIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="right" aria-label="Right"><AlignRightIcon /></ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
bad.why: The group reads and reports an array even without `multiple`, so a string `value` does not type-check and `setAlign` receives an array.

capabilities.name: segmented
capabilities.description: A number sets the gap between items in pixels. `0` also joins the items into one strip: adjoining items drop the border they share, inner corners are squared and only the strip's outer corners stay rounded (one radius step tighter when the group's own `size` is `sm`), and on a horizontal group each item's inline padding becomes `--space-2` (none for an icon-only item). The joined border is visible only with a variant that draws one (`outline`, `steel`); the `default` variant's border is transparent. Left unset, items keep a fixed `--space-1` gap and their own borders and corners.

capabilities.name: icon_only
capabilities.description: Marks every item icon-only, so each draws its glyph alone the way a standalone icon-only Toggle does.

style.description: Partially typed: CSSProperties | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property and none for this one; shape checked by tsc, see x-uikit.partially_typed_props. style is a plain React style object; when `spacing` is set, its gap replaces any gap given here. ToggleGroupProps omits Base UI's `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` style and redeclares it as React's `CSSProperties`, so the function form is not accepted; the compiler has no JSON type for `CSSProperties`, so nothing is asserted. The kit's own styling goes through toggle-group.module.css, not through this.

defaultValue.description: TS: readonly Value[] | undefined. Not fully expressible in JSON Schema; what the type states beyond the kind above is checked by tsc. defaultValue is an array of the caller's own Value type parameter, the initially pressed items. Same `readonly Value[]` type as `value`, for the uncontrolled starting state; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so the caller's narrowing is checked by tsc, not by the schema.

onValueChange.description: TS: ((groupValue: Value[], eventDetails: { reason: "none"; event: Event; cancel: () => void; allowPropagation: () => void; isCanceled: boolean; isPropagationAllowed: boolean; trigger: Element | undefined; }) => void) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. onValueChange is a callback of the next array of pressed item values and event details. Base UI types it as `(groupValue: Value[], eventDetails) => void`; a function has no JSON Schema representation, so nothing beyond its presence is asserted.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ToggleGroupState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the group's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.
